Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up for questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Hospitals Inc.'s financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key aspects: initiatives to improve operating margin, labor costs as a percentage of revenue, same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, and the status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures. These areas underscore our disciplined approach to driving sustainable growth in a challenging healthcare landscape.

Our initiatives to improve operating margin have gained significant traction, with meaningful progress that positions us for continued expansion. We've made strides in managing labor costs relative to revenue, reflecting our focus on productivity amid industry-wide pressures. Volume growth in same-facility admissions and patient days has been resilient, supporting top-line momentum. We're providing clear guidance on operating margins looking ahead, and our M&A pipeline remains robust as we optimize our portfolio.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results and expand on these priorities.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for Q3 2024 was $2.5 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved acuity, and a favorable payer mix.

Our operating expenses were $2.2 billion, representing 88% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in labor productivity and supply chain optimization. Net income for the quarter was $225 million, or $1.42 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Let me dive deeper into the five key aspects Michael highlighted, starting with our initiatives to improve operating margin—a core pillar of our 2024 strategic priorities here at Apex Hospitals. For context, our consolidated operating margin reached 9.2% in the quarter, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 5.9% and marking our strongest quarterly performance since pre-pandemic levels. This improvement drove $185 million in incremental operating income on $2.8 billion in revenue, despite persistent inflationary pressures on labor and supplies. Looking back, our margins bottomed at 4.1% in Q1 2022 amid COVID surges and RN shortages, but disciplined execution has delivered a cumulative 510 basis point recovery over the past eight quarters.

Our margin improvement framework rests on four interconnected levers: labor productivity, supply chain optimization, revenue cycle management, and high-margin service line growth. We've embedded these into our enterprise-wide MarginMax program, which has already yielded $420 million in run-rate savings and revenue uplift annualized. On labor productivity—historically our largest opex line at 52% of total costs—we've reduced agency RN spend by 35% quarter-over-quarter, from 12% of total nursing hours to under 8%, through our proprietary StaffSmart AI platform, which uses predictive analytics to forecast census and optimize float pool deployment across our 45-hospital footprint. This mirrors efficiencies seen at peers like HCA Healthcare, where similar tech has stabilized nurse turnover below 15%. We've also rolled out incentive-based scheduling in our Midwest division—eight states with heavy Medicaid exposure—cutting overtime by 22% and boosting full-time equivalent productivity to 5.8 adjusted patient days per FTE, up from 5.2 last year. Regionally, this has been transformative in rural markets like our Kansas and Nebraska facilities, where we've partnered with local travel nurse agencies under fixed-rate contracts, shielding us from the 20-25% wage inflation still plaguing coastal competitors.

On supply chain discipline, supplies represent 18% of costs, and we've captured $110 million in savings year-to-date via our deepened alliance with Vizient's supply chain consortium—similar to Universal Health Services' model. Key wins include standardizing high-volume implants for our ortho service line, reducing cost per case by 12% through competitive bidding on products like Zimmer Biomet's Persona knee systems. We've also implemented vendor-managed inventory for pharmaceuticals, trimming waste on high-cost infusibles like Remicade biosimilars by 15%. In the Southeast, where hurricane disruptions hit hard last year, our regional distribution hubs in Atlanta and Charlotte have improved on-time delivery to 98%, avoiding $25 million in expedited freight costs.

Third, our revenue cycle management enhancements are leveraging Cerner's Revenue Cycle Analytics—post our 2023 EHR harmonization—to drive a 10-day reduction in days sales outstanding to 38 days system-wide, accelerating cash conversion by $220 million. Denial rates on commercial claims dropped 40% to 4.2%, thanks to AI-powered coding audits that flagged under-documented DRGs, lifting our case mix index to 1.85 from 1.72. This is especially accretive in our West Coast markets, where Medicare Advantage penetration hit 32%—up from 25%—amid CMS's 2.9% IPPS update and favorable star ratings. We've also accelerated prior auth automation with Change Healthcare's platform, capturing 8% more elective volume like joint replacements, which carry 25-30% higher margins than medical admissions.

Finally, strategic service line repositioning has shifted 15% of our inpatient volume to outpatient and ambulatory surgery centers, growing ASC revenue 28% year-over-year to $450 million. High-margin procedures in cardiology—think TAVR volumes up 18% via partnerships with Edwards Lifesciences—and oncology infusions have offset softer COVID testing revenue. In urban clusters like our Dallas-Fort Worth system, we've launched One-Day Ortho protocols, reducing average length of stay by 0.8 days to 4.1, directly boosting throughput and margins to 14% in those facilities versus 7% system average.

Looking forward, these initiatives position us to deliver 10-12% operating margins by year-end 2025, assuming stable reimbursement and easing labor dynamics. Risks like CMS's proposed 0.3% outpatient cut or supply deflation delays are mitigated by our $500 million cost transformation buffer and flexible capex at 4% of revenue. We're also piloting value-based care bundles with UnitedHealthcare in three markets, targeting 200 basis points of upside from shared savings. MarginMax isn't a one-off; it's our operating playbook, delivering sustainable, double-digit returns on invested capital in line with industry leaders like Tenet Healthcare.

Building on that, let's turn to labor costs as a percentage of revenue, which remains the single largest component of our cost structure, typically accounting for 55% to 60% of total operating expenses in the acute care hospital sector, and it's under intense scrutiny given the ongoing dynamics in the healthcare labor market. For Q3, labor costs came in at 57.1% of revenue, a 140 basis point improvement from 58.5% in the prior-year quarter and a 90 basis point sequential decline from Q2's 58.0%. On an absolute basis, labor expenses grew 4.2% year-over-year to $1.28 billion, driven primarily by a 6.1% increase in average hourly wages across our 42,000 FTEs. However, this growth was more than offset by revenue expansion of 8.7% to $2.24 billion, fueled by a 3.2% rise in adjusted patient days and a 1.8% uptick in our case mix index to 1.72—reflecting stronger acuity from our focus on high-margin orthopedics and cardiology procedures.

To give you a granular breakdown, nursing labor—which represents about 42% of our total labor spend—improved to 24.3% of revenue from 25.1% a year ago, thanks to targeted productivity gains. Physician labor, including both employed and contracted providers, held steady at 14.8%, while administrative and support roles ticked down to 18.0% from 18.6%. Premium labor, or agency and contract staffing, was a bright spot at just 2.7% of revenue, down from 4.1% last year—a testament to our aggressive de-dependency strategy.

Let me contextualize the trends. The broader industry has seen labor costs balloon to 59-62% of revenue for peers like Community Health Systems and Tenet Healthcare, per their recent filings, amid a national RN vacancy rate hovering at 15-18% according to NSI Nursing Solutions data. Wage inflation persists at 5-7% annually, exacerbated by union activity—we've navigated three successful contracts this year without concessions—and burnout from post-COVID volumes. In our portfolio, we've seen pockets of pressure: Southeast facilities, which comprise 35% of our 28-hospital footprint, held labor at a favorable 56.2% due to lower regional wage baselines and strong local talent pipelines from programs like those at Emory and Vanderbilt. Conversely, our West Coast markets—particularly California, 12% of revenue—ran hotter at 60.4%, influenced by AB 2579 staffing mandates and seismic retrofitting costs that indirectly inflate overtime.

Strategically, we're not just managing this; we're transforming it. We've rolled out next-gen workforce optimization tech, including UKG Pro Workforce Management—formerly Kronos—across 85% of our facilities, which has slashed scheduling inefficiencies by 22% and reduced overtime by 15% quarter-over-quarter. Early pilots of AI-driven predictive staffing from Qventus are yielding 10-12% productivity lifts per FTE, projecting $25 million in annualized savings by Q4 2024. On the retention front, our Caregiver Commitment program—$50 million invested year-to-date in bonuses, tuition reimbursement, and mental health sabbaticals—has boosted nurse retention to 88% from 82% last year, outpacing HCA Healthcare's 85% benchmark.

Regionally, we're tailoring approaches: In the Midwest, partnerships with AMN Healthcare and Cross Country have stabilized contract rates 18% below national averages, while our Texas and Florida assets benefit from right-to-work laws and migration inflows, keeping labor under 55%. Looking ahead to value-based care under MSSP and CJR bundles, we're upskilling FTEs for episodic payment models, which should further delever labor intensity as telehealth visits—now 28% of outpatient encounters via our Epic MyChart integration—reduce bedside staffing needs by 8-10% per shift. For Q4 guidance, we expect labor as a percentage of revenue to range 56.5% to 57.5%, assuming continued CMI stability and no material escalation in agency rates. This positions us for 50-75 basis points of margin expansion in FY24, aligning with our 5-7% EBITDA growth target. We're confident these initiatives not only mitigate the structural headwinds but drive sustainable outperformance versus the 1-2% industry average labor productivity growth.

Next, on same-facility admissions and patient days growth, both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter. These metrics are core to our same-store performance, excluding the impact of our recent divestitures in the Midwest and the two de novo facilities we brought online in Q4 2023. We're reporting on a same-facility base of 185 acute care hospitals and 42 freestanding ERs, representing about 92% of our consolidated footprint.

Starting with the headline numbers: Same-facility admissions grew 2.8% year-over-year, marking our sixth straight quarter of positive year-over-year volume growth and accelerating from 1.9% in Q1. Patient days came in even stronger at 3.4% year-over-year, driven by a modest uptick in acuity and length of stay. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, admissions were down 0.9%, while patient days dipped 1.2%—in line with typical seasonal softness post-winter respiratory season and ahead of summer elective procedure ramps.

Year-over-year drivers were broad-based across service lines, led by a robust 5.2% increase in surgical admissions, reflecting pent-up demand for high-margin elective procedures like orthopedics and cardiology. Our case mix index rose 1.7% year-over-year to 1.68, fueled by strength in complex cases—think cardiac ablations, neurointerventional procedures, and oncology infusions—partly due to our $250 million investment in 2023 for hybrid OR suites and da Vinci Xi robotic systems across 60 facilities. Medical admissions grew a more modest 1.1% year-over-year, tempered by ongoing shifts to observation stays and outpatient alternatives, but we saw solid uptake in our post-acute transition programs, which helped stabilize volumes.

Patient days benefited from a 0.6-day extension in average length of stay to 4.7 days, attributable to higher acuity patients requiring extended ICU and step-down care. This was particularly evident in our behavioral health segment, where patient days surged 7.1% year-over-year amid national mental health crises and expanded bed capacity from our 2022 Spectrum Health acquisition integration.

Regionally, performance was polarized. Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas, which comprise 55% of our same-facility bed capacity—drove 4.1% year-over-year admissions growth, outpacing the national average. Florida alone delivered 5.8% growth, boosted by Medicare fee-for-service tailwinds from an aging demographic and our new payer contracts with Humana and UnitedHealthcare, which include value-based incentives for bundled ortho episodes. In contrast, our Northeast and Midwest clusters grew just 0.7% year-over-year, pressured by Medicaid redeterminations post-pandemic unwind and aggressive Medicare Advantage denials. We've seen Medicare Advantage denial rates climb to 18% from 12% a year ago, echoing industry-wide trends reported by peers like HCA and UHS, hitting low-acuity medical admissions hardest.

Quarter-over-quarter dynamics reflect seasonality and operational resets. Admissions declined 0.9% from Q1's elevated flu/COVID peak, with patient days down 1.2% due to a 0.3-day length-of-stay contraction as elective volumes normalized post-Lent and spring break. Notably, our observation-adjusted admissions metric—net of less-than-24-hour stays—only fell 0.4% quarter-over-quarter, signaling underlying strength in true inpatient demand.

From a technical standpoint, several initiatives underpinned this resilience. Our enterprise-wide Epic MyChart implementation, now live in 85% of facilities, has improved patient throughput by 12% via AI-driven bed management tools from Qventus, reducing discharge delays by 18 hours on average. We've also leaned into tele-stroke and tele-ICU partnerships with CerebraHealth, expanding our neuroscience service line and capturing 15% more transfer admissions year-over-year. Capacity utilization sits at 68%—up 200 basis points year-over-year—giving us runway for the second half growth without straining staffing ratios.

Strategically, we're positioning for sustained mid-single-digit volume growth. We're accelerating high-acuity investments, including $150 million in 2024 for 20 new neuro-ICU beds and partnerships with Blue Cross Blue Shield for cardiology centers of excellence. To counter Medicare Advantage headwinds, we've renegotiated 70% of our Medicare Advantage contracts with upstream appeals processes and launched a dedicated prior-auth team, projecting a 300 basis points case mix index lift by year-end. Looking ahead, we guide to 3-4% year-over-year same-facility admissions growth for Q4 and full-year, with patient days at 3.5-4.5%, assuming stable payer mix and no major COVID resurgence. Overall, these results affirm our market-share gains in a fragmented industry, where we're outperforming the 1.5% national inpatient utilization growth per CMS data.

Turning to operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, as this has been a focal point for many of you. Operating margins remain a critical metric in our industry, especially amid ongoing reimbursement pressures from CMS's Medicare Physician Fee Schedule cuts, escalating labor costs driven by the national nursing shortage, and supply chain inflation that's lingered post-pandemic.

To recap, for the full-year-to-date 2024, we've delivered adjusted operating margins trending toward 12.8%, up from prior periods, driven by same-facility revenue growth fueled by pent-up elective procedure demand—orthopedics, cardiology, and neurosurgery volumes exceeding expectations—and a favorable payer mix shift toward commercial patients. We also realized net cost savings through enterprise-wide initiatives, including labor productivity gains from our AI-powered workforce management platform in partnership with ShiftMed and optimized staffing models at our 45 acute care facilities.

That said, we've faced headwinds: consolidated labor costs rose due to wage inflation averaging 5.5% for RNs and elevated contract labor premiums in high-demand markets like Florida and Texas. Medical supply costs were up, though we've clawed back through our group purchasing organization synergies with Vizient. Reimbursement dynamics were mixed—Medicare Advantage denials ticked up, but our value-based care contracts delivered margin accretion.

For Q4 2024, we are guiding adjusted operating margins to 13.5% to 14.0%, representing 70 to 120 basis points of expansion sequentially. For full-year 2024, we expect margins of 14.2% to 14.8%, implying roughly 140 to 200 basis points of year-over-year growth.

Key drivers include volume and acuity trends: We're forecasting same-facility admissions growth of 3.0% to 3.5% in Q4, with case mix index stable at 1.82 to 1.85, underpinned by continued elective recovery—at 98% of pre-COVID volumes—and outpatient momentum, where our ambulatory surgery centers saw strong growth. Sunbelt regions, comprising 65% of our bed capacity—our Florida and Texas clusters—will lead with 4.5% volume growth, benefiting from population in-migration. Northeast markets may lag due to softer commercial volumes and Medicaid redeterminations.

Pricing and reimbursement: Net revenue per admission expected to grow 2.5% to 3.0%, with commercial pricing up on annual contract renewals. Flat Medicare reimbursement after the IPPS update, offset by Medicare Advantage drag, but our revenue cycle management tech stack—enhanced with Change Healthcare's AI denial prediction engine and Epic modules rolled out across 90% of hospitals—should drive days in A/R down, adding 50 basis points to margins.

Cost discipline: Labor expense growth guided to 4.5% to 5.0%, below industry averages, thanks to 15% reduction in traveler usage via internal float pools and partnerships with Incredible Health. Non-labor costs pegged at 3.0% growth, moderated by our Oracle Health supply chain analytics. We're targeting $220 million in total cost reductions for 2024, including facility rationalization.

Strategic initiatives amplifying margins: Full deployment of our telehealth platform with Teladoc, covering 30% of outpatient visits, reducing inpatient length-of-stay and boosting throughput. Scaling bundled payment arrangements to 28% of episodes, targeting ortho and cardiology with Blue Cross Blue Shield for 300+ basis points uplift. Closing our acquisition of high-margin ASCs and breaking ground on micro-hospitals. Investments in renewable energy and sepsis prediction AI, cutting readmissions.

Risks include prolonged labor strikes, CMS site-neutral proposals, or cyber risks—we've stress-tested and carry insurance. Assuming no recessionary pullback, this positions us to outperform the industry median.

Finally, an update on the status of ongoing or planned acquisitions and divestitures, which remain a cornerstone of our capital allocation strategy. In this dynamic environment—marked by labor cost inflation averaging 5-7% year-over-year, Medicare reimbursement pressures from the FY2025 IPPS final rule, and demand for high-acuity outpatient services driven by an aging demographic and Medicare Advantage shifts to 35% of our mix—our M&A playbook focuses on bolstering our core acute care footprint in high-growth Sunbelt markets, accelerating our pivot to ambulatory and value-based care, and pruning non-core, low-margin assets to optimize for 12-15% adjusted EBITDA margins. We've deployed $1.2 billion in M&A year-to-date, funded through cash flows from operations—up 8%—and our Term Loan B issuance.

Recently completed: In late August, we closed our $425 million acquisition of Southeast Regional Health Partners, a three-hospital system with 850 beds across Georgia and South Carolina. Accretive at 14% EBITDA margins, strong service lines, and payer mix. Synergies tracking at $28 million annualized from supply chain and Epic harmonization. Also, three tuck-in ASC acquisitions totaling $180 million in Texas and Florida, adding 12 facilities and $95 million revenue at over 35% margins.

Ongoing: Late-stage discussions for $650 million acquisition of Midwest Specialty Hospitals, a five-facility LTACH and IRF network—immediately 15-20% EPS accretive at 7.8x EBITDA. On track for Q1 2025 close.

Planned: $1.1 billion bid for Coastal Behavioral Health, 12-hospital platform adding 1,200 beds in mental health. And $300 million for 8-10 ASC and home health bolt-ons in the Southwest.

Divestitures: Sold three underperforming rural facilities in Pennsylvania and Kentucky for $210 million—recycled proceeds into SRHP. This boosts urban concentration and occupancy.

We expect M&A to contribute 200-250 basis points to FY2025 EPS growth, with $2.5-3 billion deployment. Risks around rates and FTC scrutiny, but our track record is strong.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our integrated care pathway program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, including telehealth expansions and AI-driven predictive tools for sepsis and staffing that tie directly into our operational efficiencies.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the StaffSmart AI platform on your revenue growth and the impact on hospital efficiency?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, David. Great question. The StaffSmart AI platform has been transformative, as Lisa touched on. By reducing agency RN spend 35% quarter-over-quarter and boosting FTE productivity to 5.8 adjusted patient days per FTE, it's directly supported revenue growth through higher throughput—contributing to our 2.8% same-facility admissions increase. On efficiency, it's cut overtime 22% in key divisions and stabilized turnover, mirroring HCA's gains, which has freed up capacity for more high-margin electives and lifted overall hospital utilization to 68%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Kim:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, Jennifer. Our expansion plans align tightly with our M&A strategy Lisa outlined. We're prioritizing Sunbelt markets, with the recent Southeast Regional Health Partners acquisition adding 850 beds and ASC tuck-ins in Texas and Florida boosting ambulatory capacity. Looking ahead, the pipeline includes the Midwest Specialty Hospitals deal and Coastal Behavioral Health for behavioral health scale, plus de novo micro-hospitals. This will grow our footprint by 10-15% while targeting 12-15% EBITDA margins, focusing on high-growth areas with favorable demographics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Absolutely, Mark. We're leveraging Epic MyChart across 85% of facilities for 12% better throughput, Qventus AI for bed management reducing discharge delays by 18 hours, and CerebraHealth for tele-stroke and tele-ICU, capturing 15% more transfers. Additionally, Change Healthcare for prior auth automation and Cerner's analytics have cut DSO to 38 days and denials to 4.2%, enhancing coordination from admission to post-acute transitions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks. On your margin guidance, how are you thinking about potential Medicare Advantage denial risks into next year?

Lisa Chen:
Good question, Alex. We've baked in Medicare Advantage headwinds, with denials up to 18%, but our renegotiated contracts covering 70% include upstream appeals, and dedicated prior-auth teams project 300 bps CMI lift. RCM enhancements add 50 bps, and VBC bundles target 200-300 bps upside. We're guiding 14.2-14.8% for full-year 2024 with buffers for reimbursement stability.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Dr. Reynolds for closing remarks.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
